text:
Maya K: Quick Q — for the async job endpoint (/v1/jobs) what do we guarantee for polling semantics and cancels? Want to make the SDK behavior consistent across hosted/dedicated/private.
Linus: Good call. Are you thinking about status shape, HTTP codes, and headers for backoff?
Maya K: Yup. Also how clients should handle duplicate request IDs and client retries. We should be explicit about when to return 202 vs 200 vs 404 for cancels.
Priya: From infra side: cancel should be idempotent and return 200 if already canceled or finished? But 204 is also reasonable for a successful cancel with no body.
Shaun: my vote: POST /v1/jobs -> 202 + Location header (/v1/jobs/:id). Polling GET returns 200 with status body. Cancel endpoint should be POST /v1/jobs/:id/cancel -> 202 if cancel accepted, 200 if already terminal, 404 if unknown id.
Maya K: I want us to avoid too many different codes for the SDK. Maybe canonicalize to: create -> 202, poll -> 200 always (with status field), cancel -> 200 (body shows outcome). Use headers for backoff: `Retry-After` optional.
Linus: Agree on single poll 200. For cancel: returning 200 always simplifies client logic. Provide `status` in body: `cancelling` -> transition -> `cancelled` or `failed`.
Priya: We should define the status schema clearly. Proposal:
```
{
  "job_id": "string",
  "status": "queued|running|succeeded|failed|cancelled|cancelling",
  "progress": 0,
  "eta_seconds": 30, // nullable
  "result_url": "string|null"
}
```
Linus: +1. Also include `x-request-id` in responses so client can correlate retries.
Shaun: On duplicate request IDs: server should return the same job id if a client re-sends the same idempotency key within retention window. SDK should expose a `create_or_get` semantic.
Maya K: How long for that retention window? This affects clients that crash and retry later.
Priya: Ops suggests 24 hours by default for hosted plans, configurable for Dedicated. We'll document it.
Linus: Polling backoff suggestion: naive retry every 500ms for first 2s, then exponential to a max of 10s. Use `Retry-After` to override.
Maya K: Good. Edge case: if client polls after `result_url` expires, return 410? Or 200 with `result_url: null` and `status: succeeded` plus a note?
Shaun: Prefer 200 with `result_url: null` and an additional `notes` field explaining expiry to avoid forcing special-casing 410.
Linus: Also add `last_update_ts` so clients can detect staleness.
Priya: Security note: cancel should require the original auth token or owner scope; don't allow cross-tenant cancels.
Maya K: Action items: Linus — update API spec with status schema + headers. Shaun — PR in SDK to normalize cancel -> always 200 body-based outcome. Priya — add retention config docs for Dedicated.
Shaun: I'll ping codeowners and submit a small spec PR today. @Maya K can you add the SDK acceptance tests you'd like?
Maya K: Yes, I'll drop test cases in the spec PR: idempotent create, poll transitions, cancel idempotency, retry-after handling.
infra-bot: Reminder: job retention defaults: hosted=24h, dedicated=custom, private=customer-managed. See https://infra.internal/jobs-retention
Priya: Cool, I'll update the admin docs once spec lands.
Maya K: Thanks all :tada!
